description:
Project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)

Context at Redwood Inference:
Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and isolation. Today, scaling behavior is mostly platform-driven (reactive signals + operator overrides). Enterprise Dedicated customers increasingly need explicit contractual/operational guardrails: hard min/max capacity bounds (to control spend and ensure baseline SLOs) plus “predictive” scaling signals (to avoid cold-start/queue buildup during known traffic ramps).

Goals:
1) Customer-configurable autoscaling bounds: enforce min/max replicas (and/or GPU quota) per Dedicated deployment, with clear precedence over platform defaults.
2) Predictive scaling signals: optionally bias scaling decisions using forecasted demand (time-of-day patterns, scheduled events, historical rate/latency), while respecting bounds.
3) Safety + reliability: avoid oscillation, prevent scale-down below safe baseline, and provide deterministic behavior under conflicting signals.
4) Operability: dashboards, alerts, and runbooks for scaling behavior; auditability of config changes and scaling decisions.
5) Customer experience: expose bounds and predictive mode in Console/API, document semantics, and provide CS/support playbooks.

In scope:
- Control plane schema for per-deployment scaling policy (min/max, cooldowns, predictive mode, fallback to reactive).
- Fleet autoscaler changes to enforce bounds and incorporate predictive signal pipeline.
- Observability: metrics for desired vs bounded capacity, prediction error, scale events, saturation, and queue depth.
- Rollout: feature flagging by account/deployment, canary in one region, gradual expansion to select Dedicated customers, then GA.

Out of scope (initially):
- Cross-region active-active predictive placement optimization.
- Dynamic contract renegotiation flows (handled by Sales/CS outside product).
- Fully automated procurement workflows based on predictions.

Primary stakeholders:
- Product (Dedicated): Lauren Bishop (DRI for product requirements, GA criteria)
- Platform Control Plane: Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee (config/policy API + validation)
- Fleet/Infrastructure: Vanessa Ortiz, Keiko Yamamoto (autoscaler + guardrails)
- SRE: Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton (reliability, on-call readiness, incident playbooks)
- Observability: Allison Grant, Sergio Costa (dashboards/alerts)
- Smart Routing integration (capacity signals consumers): Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon
- Customer Success / Support: escalation handling, customer comms, enablement materials

Phases & timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): customer discovery + requirements, define semantics (bounds precedence, failure modes)
- Phase 1 (2–3 weeks): design docs + ADRs, API/schema finalized, observability plan
- Phase 2 (4–6 weeks): implementation (control plane + autoscaler + signals), unit/integration tests, simulation tooling
- Phase 3 (2–3 weeks): canary rollout, SRE readiness review, customer pilot, fix-forward
- Phase 4 (1–2 weeks): GA launch, docs, CS enablement, post-launch monitoring/retro

Key deliverables:
- PRD + design spec + ADR(s)
- Implemented policy enforcement and predictive mode
- Dashboards/alerts/runbooks
- Customer-facing docs updates and support playbooks

Constraints & considerations:
- Hard safety invariants: never exceed max, never drop below min, preserve tenant isolation, avoid thundering herd on scale-up.
- Deterministic policy evaluation (auditability): record “requested desired”, “bounded desired”, and “why”.
- Backward compatibility: existing customers retain current behavior until enabled.
- Multi-signal arbitration: reactive saturation/queue depth must override prediction when prediction is wrong, but still respect bounds.
- Compliance: config changes must be logged (who/when/what), especially for enterprise customers.

files.description: PRD for Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode: customer problems, personas, requirements, non-goals, success metrics (SLO/latency, cost), rollout plan, GA criteria.
Design spec for control plane schema and Console UX: fields (min/max, cooldowns, predictive toggle), validation rules, UX mocks described in text, migration/backward compatibility.
ADR defining semantics and precedence: how min/max interacts with platform defaults, overload behavior, scale-down safety, and conflict resolution with predictive/reactive signals.
End-to-end architecture: fleet autoscaler changes, signal ingestion, prediction service interface, rate limits, failure modes, and region-by-region rollout approach.
Service doc for capacity/scaling policy evaluation in the control plane: APIs, storage, caching, audit logging, ownership, and SLO expectations.
SLO/alerting updates for Dedicated scaling: new indicators (queue depth, bounded capacity hit-rate), paging thresholds, error budget policy during rollout.
Dashboard spec: panels for desired vs bounded replicas, prediction vs actual demand, scale event timelines, saturation signals, and per-customer drilldowns.
Runbook for on-call/SRE: diagnosing stuck scale-up/down, max-bound saturation, prediction pipeline outages, safe mitigations, and escalation paths.
CS/support playbook: questions to ask customers, how to interpret bounded scaling metrics, common misconfigs, and guidance on choosing min/max.
Known issues list for predictive mode: false positives, timezone misalignment, insufficient history, rollout caveats, and recommended workarounds.
Standardization doc for new scaling metrics: naming conventions, labels (customer_id, deployment_id, region), and cardinality limits.
Release notes entry for the feature: what changed, how to enable, migration notes, and links to docs/runbooks.
Working notes from customer interviews: pain points (budget caps, baseline capacity), desired semantics, and quotes to support PRD.
Early PRD draft with open questions, rough scope, and iteration history before formal Confluence PRD.
Spreadsheet-style doc: candidate signals, expected lead times, data sources, and a scoring matrix for usefulness vs complexity.
Simulation write-up: replay historical traffic, compare reactive vs predictive, quantify overshoot/undershoot and time-to-recover; includes charts described in text.
Step-by-step migration plan for existing Dedicated deployments: defaulting behavior, opt-in flag, safe rollbacks.
Schema scratchpad: JSON examples, validation rules, RBAC considerations, and notes about backwards compatibility.
Draft dashboard layout + alert ideas; notes about avoiding high-cardinality labels and what CS needs for QBRs.
SRE readiness review checklist: runbook completeness, alerts tested, game day plan, and launch gating items.
Brainstorm doc: buy vs build forecasting; interfaces, SLAs for prediction service, and fallback behavior if forecasts are stale.
Launch brief draft: customer messaging, enablement checklist, internal comms, and post-launch monitoring plan.
Enumerated edge cases: min>max, rapid config churn, region capacity shortages, partial outages, and how autoscaler should behave.
Notes defining audit log events for scaling policy changes and autoscaler decisions; fields needed for compliance reviews.
PM epic tracking the initiative: milestones (schema, autoscaler, observability, pilot, GA), customer pilot list, and GA exit criteria.
Engineering ticket for autoscaler enforcement of min/max; includes subtasks, risk notes, and links to design/ADR.
Ticket for control plane API/schema changes: new fields, migrations, validation, RBAC, and audit logging requirements.
Ticket for integrating forecast inputs: data pipeline, staleness checks, feature flag, and fallback to reactive scaling.
Ticket defining/implementing metrics and logs: desired vs bounded, bound-hit counters, prediction error metrics.
Console work item: form fields, guardrails, preview of cost/capacity impact, and per-deployment enablement.
SRE/observability ticket: alert thresholds, paging routing, and integration with on-call runbooks.
Ticket to emit audit events: who changed bounds, autoscaler decision reasoning, and retention requirements for enterprise.
Ticket to validate predictive scaling via replay/sim: scenarios, acceptance thresholds, and regression test harness.
Ticket for gating and rollout controls: per-account flags, safe defaults, and rollback mechanisms.
Ticket to produce docs and CS materials: support macros, configuration guidance, and troubleshooting steps.
Design ticket for UX flows and validation states (min/max errors, warnings, prediction confidence display).
Decision-focused ticket: define which bounds are hard enforced vs suggested, and how UI communicates “platform recommended range.”
Ticket addressing shortage edge case: how to surface unmet min, alerting, and customer communications.
Pilot plan: candidate accounts, success criteria, comms cadence, and feedback collection process.
IaC support ticket: expose bounds/predictive mode via redwood-terraform provider modules; examples and docs.
Migration ticket: set implicit defaults, ensure no behavior changes until enabled, and backfill audit trails.
Game day ticket: failure injection scenarios (forecast outage, spike, stuck scale-down), roles, and success criteria.
PR adding control plane schema fields for min/max bounds and predictive mode toggles; includes validation and migration scaffolding.
PR implementing hard enforcement in autoscaler loop: clamp desired replicas, emit bound-hit metrics, and add tests for edge cases.
PR adding forecast provider interface, staleness checks, and fallback logic to reactive scaling when predictions are unavailable.
PR adding audit events for scaling decisions and config changes; includes event schema and integration with logging pipeline.
PR adding metrics and structured logs for desired/bounded capacity, prediction error, and scale-event reasons.
PR exposing new endpoints to Console for reading/updating scaling policy; includes RBAC checks and input validation.
PR implementing account/deployment-scoped feature flags and safe rollbacks for predictive mode.
PR improving behavior when min capacity can’t be provisioned: surface degraded state, alerts, and retry backoff.
PR adding a simulation/replay harness to evaluate scaling outcomes using historical traces; outputs summary stats.
PR adding cooldowns, dampening, and minimum step sizing to reduce oscillation under noisy predictive inputs.
PR adding migrations/backfills to preserve existing behavior until opt-in; includes migration safety checks.
PR improving validation error messages returned to Console (min>max, invalid cooldown) and adding integration tests.
PR adding Grafana dashboards for bound-hit rate, queue depth, prediction error, and scale event timelines.
PR adding alert rules and notification routing for max-bound saturation + sustained queue buildup.
PR adding canary test scenarios (traffic ramps, periodic spikes) to validate predictive mode doesn’t regress latency.
PR updating Terraform modules/provider examples to configure scaling bounds and predictive mode.
PR updating customer-facing docs: how to set min/max, what predictive mode does, recommended ranges, and troubleshooting.
Hotfix PR addressing a bug discovered in pilot: null prediction leading to unsafe downscale; adds guard + test.
PR adding throttling/rate limits on repeated scaling policy updates and emitting warnings/audit events.
PR exposing bounded-capacity state to routing so it can degrade gracefully (e.g., fallback routing) without violating bounds.
PR adding an internal CLI to dump effective scaling policy, last decisions, and bound-hit history for a deployment.
PR adding internal release note + changelog entry for the Dedicated autoscaling bounds feature.
Thread coordinating autoscaler bounds implementation details: edge cases, defaulting strategy, and ownership of migration/backfill.
Thread on control plane validation rules and RBAC for scaling policy updates; includes API snippets and reviewer feedback.
Thread reviewing proposed alerts/paging thresholds for max-bound saturation; discussion about noise and customer impact.
Thread with PM/Eng clarifying semantics for predictive mode vs reactive overrides; open questions and decision proposal.
Thread referencing ADR draft: precedence ordering and determinism requirements; quick consensus and follow-ups.

On-call handoff thread: new runbook link, what to page on, and known failure modes during pilot.
Thread about interaction between batching/throughput and autoscaler signals; whether queue depth is a stable scaling metric for certain models.
Thread coordinating game day plan: scenarios, who drives, and what metrics to watch.
Thread about audit log event shape and retention; compliance considerations for enterprise Dedicated accounts.
Thread after canary rollout: early results, bound-hit rates, prediction error, and next steps for expanding pilot.
Customer ticket: requests hard max bound to prevent unexpected scale-up; includes impact, environment/region, and interim mitigation.
Customer ticket: latency/queue spikes at predictable times; asks for predictive scaling; links to dashboards and proposed pilot enrollment.
Ticket documenting shortage scenario; includes SRE notes, customer comms, and follow-up action items for degraded-state surfacing.
Ticket from pilot customer: oscillating capacity leading to jitter; includes logs, graphs, and references to hotfix PR.
Internal helpdesk ticket requesting feature flag enablement for a specific pilot account; includes approvals and rollout checklist.
Customer question ticket: guidance on choosing bounds to meet SLA; response references docs and CS playbook.
CRM company record for a Dedicated prospect (Northstar Fintech – Dedicated): requires strict cost ceilings and baseline capacity; notes mention autoscaling bounds as a close driver and a pilot plan.
CRM record for an enterprise customer: daily ramp traffic; security requirements + interest in predictive scaling; links to related Fireflies calls and support tickets.
CRM record: evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted; wants min baseline + max cap; contains evaluation timeline, competitors mentioned, next steps.
CRM record: compliance-heavy customer; wants auditability of scaling config changes; notes tie to audit logs and change management.
Discovery call transcript: customer describes budget cap + unpredictable bursts; Redwood discusses bounds semantics and rollout timeline; action items recorded.

Security review transcript: customer asks about audit logging for scaling policy changes, retention, RBAC; Redwood outlines audit events.
Procurement/legal call transcript: negotiating SLA and documenting min baseline + max ceiling; ties requirements to product feature and contract language.
Email thread: PM requests leadership/SRE approval for pilot customers and rollout plan; includes risk notes and proposed schedule.
Email thread: infra leadership review of risks when customers set high mins; discusses shortage handling, comms, and capacity planning implications.
Email thread: follow-up from a pilot incident; links to Jira ticket and GitHub hotfix PR; assigns owners and deadlines.
Email thread: enterprise customer requires IaC for bounds; coordinates eng work (redwood-terraform PR) and delivery timeline.
GA go/no-go email thread: checklist status (alerts, runbooks, docs, customer comms), open issues, and final approval decision.
